claims.text: Untreated equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a coarse-grained, single-phase BCC alloy with poor room-temperature ductility.
Untreated NbMoTaW exhibits approximately 2% compressive plasticity at room temperature.
Untreated NbMoTaW has excellent high-temperature mechanical performance.
Room-temperature severe plastic deformation increases defect density and reduces grain size.
HPT or ECAP followed by a short 600–800 °C anneal will produce a submicron-to-nanocrystalline grain structure in NbMoTaW.
A short 600–800 °C anneal can promote partial recrystallization and limited recovery without complete grain coarsening.
The proposed annealing window can avoid unwanted phase transformations in NbMoTaW.
The processed alloy will have a high density of grain boundaries at room temperature.
Increased grain-boundary area will promote grain-boundary-mediated plasticity in NbMoTaW.
Grain refinement will provide multiple dislocation sources in NbMoTaW.
The refined microstructure will improve room-temperature ductility relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
Exposure at approximately 1600 °C will coarsen the refined grains to a size similar to the untreated baseline.
High-temperature grain coarsening will restore the high-temperature strength of NbMoTaW.
SPD plus annealing will maintain the excellent mechanical performance of NbMoTaW at 1600 °C.
The recovered BCC structure will have defect-formation energies similar to those of untreated NbMoTaW.
Similar defect-formation energies in the recovered BCC structure will preserve irradiation resistance.
SPD plus annealing will maintain irradiation resistance relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
Incomplete recovery during annealing could compromise high-temperature strength.
Excessive grain growth during processing could negate the room-temperature ductility improvement.
